title:
GEOLOGIC MAP OF PART OF THE TYRRHENA
A PATERA
REGION OF MARS
(MTM QUADRANGLE -2025
By
Tracy K.P. Gregg, David A. Crown, and Ronald Greeley
1998

legend_data.value: Channel-floor material - Metalliferous material locally transversed by narrow (<500 m) ridges, <1 km wide, steep-sided, shallow-stepped valleys dissecting shield material. Observed in high resolution (>50 m/pixel) Viking Orbiter images (V045AS series). Interpretation: Deposits of reworked composite shield material and shield material deposited downslope by both erosion and deposition.

Etched plains material - Broad, flat plains with fewer more widely spaced ridges; shallow, cup-shaped scars observed parallel to and between ridges. Locally, scarp-matted with smooth deposits. Embays basal shield material. Precise origin uncertain. Erosional scars suggest non-uniform deposition. Shield material may be reworked shield material or etched plain material.

Ridged plains material - Broad, flat plains with intersecting mid-size ridges oriented northwest-southeast and northeast-southwest. Typical of northern Tharsis region north of Tyrrhena Patera summit area, outside map area. Embays basal shield material north, east, and south of Tyrrhena Patera. Interpretation: Late-stage lava flows formed ridged plains material.

Ridged and etched plains material - Broad, flat plains with intersecting mid-size ridges oriented northwest-southeast and northeast-southwest. Ridges are embayed by younger shield material or modified ridged plains material.

Rille-floor material - Surface located within two elliptical depressions and rille at Tyrrhena Patera summit area. Rilles continue southeastward toward main map area and join in a 1000 m wide depression near the center of the map area, which are aligned roughly parallel to radial lines from Tyrrhena Patera summit. Rilles cross all shield materials. Lava flows fill most of the rille floor. Rilles are typically 5-10 km wide, with broad (>5 km) flat-floored channels radiating outward from Tyrrhena Patera summit. Contains arcuate graben, crater chains, and other features typical of rilled plains material.

Upper shield material - Smooth (at >50 m pixel resolution) surface continues on and around Tyrrhena Patera summit region. Consists of basaltic shield material. Formed by successive lava flows that filled pre-existing topography. Thin, steep-sided, flat-floored channels radiating outward from Tyrrhena Patera summit. Contains arcuate graben, crater chains, and other features typical of rilled plains material.

Lower shield material - Smooth to moderately hummocky surface form positive relief spurs and isolated, short-stepped ridges surrounded by broad (>5 km) flat-floored channels. Forms of broad shield material include some broad shield material and some shield material. Steep-sided, flat-floored channels radiating outward from Tyrrhena Patera summit. Contains arcuate graben, crater chains, and other features typical of rilled plains material.

Basal shield material - Smooth surface form positive relief spurs and isolated, short-stepped ridges surrounded by broad (>5 km) flat-floored channels. Forms of broad shield material include some broad shield material and some shield material. Steep-sided, flat-floored channels radiating outward from Tyrrhena Patera summit. Contains arcuate graben, crater chains, and other features typical of rilled plains material.

Well-preserved crater material - Characterized by pronounced, continuous, raised rim elevated relative to surrounding materials and well-defined interior. Interpreted as pristinely preserved crater material with little degradation.

Moderately degraded crater material - Characterized by a crater rim that is discontinuous, poorly defined, and exhibits moderate to severe degradation. Impact craters showing moderate to severe degradation.

Highly degraded crater material - Characterized by a crater rim that is discontinuous and exhibits little relief relative to surrounding materials. No ejecta, no obvious ejecta blanket. Most heavily degraded craters may be covered by young materials, such as volcanic deposits.
Mare-type wrinkle ridge—Showing crest. Represents contact in places
Arcuate or linear ridge crest—Represents contact in places
